refnamediv.refpurpose: Identify unique poles in p and their associated multiplicity.

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: [multp, idxp] = mpoles(p) [multp, idxp] = mpoles(p, tol) [multp, idxp] = mpoles(p, tol, reorder)

listitem.para: Vector of poles (single or double floating-point values).
(optional) Tolerance for identifying multiple poles. If the relative difference of two poles is less than `tol`, they are considered multiples. Default is 0.001.
(optional) Logical or numeric scalar. If `%t` (default), poles are sorted from largest to smallest magnitude. If `%f`, poles are not sorted.
Vector specifying the multiplicity of the poles. `multp(n)` refers to the multiplicity of the Nth pole `p(idxp(n))`.
Indices of the poles in the original vector `p`, ordered by magnitude (if `reorder` is `%t`).

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: The `mpoles` function identifies unique poles in the input vector `p` and determines their multiplicity. Poles are considered multiples if their relative difference is less than the specified tolerance `tol`. By default, the poles are sorted in descending order of magnitude. If `reorder` is set to `%f`, the poles are not sorted. Notes
- If `tol` is not provided, the default value of 0.001 is used. - If `reorder` is not provided, the poles are sorted by default.
